item.title: College Tennis Over the Years
item.dc:creator: Halle Winfrey
item.description:
There are over 1,100 teams that make up the women’s college tennis league, consisting of Division I, II, and III within the NCAA. All of these teams are made up of talented players who compete to get to the NCAA Women’s College Tennis Championships.

But, with these different teams, which has been the best college team from the past four seasons? Which has had the highest amount of points?

To find the top teams in the league, we will use the total number of points from each team, which consist of points, games and sets; which is how each team’s total is scored.

Next, to find the number one team, we will filter out any team who has less than 57 total points, since there are so many teams, which leaves us with a total of 38 teams looking at each season back to 2022.

Let’s see the results.

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(ggbump)
library(ggrepel)
library(gt)
library(ggnewscale)

womens <- read_csv("Women's Tennis - Sheet1.csv") |> mutate(Team = gsub(" (M)", "", Team, fixed=TRUE))

high <- womens |> 
  arrange(desc(Points))

best <- womens |> filter(Points > 57)
UTA <- womens |> filter(Team == "University of Texas at Austin")
WF <- womens |> filter(Team == "Wake Forest")
OS <- womens |> filter(Team == "Ohio State")

beststacked <- best |> 
  separate(`W - L`, into=c("Wins", "Losses"), sep=" - ") |> 
  mutate(
    Wins = as.numeric(Wins),
    Losses = as.numeric(Losses)
  ) |> 
  group_by(Team) |> 
  summarize(
    Wins = sum(Wins),
    Losses = sum(Losses)
  ) |> 
  arrange(desc(Wins)) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Team,
    names_to = "Outcome",
    values_to = "Total"
  ) 

beststacked$Outcome <- factor(beststacked$Outcome, levels = c("Wins", "Losses"))

OSLong <- beststacked |> filter(Team == "Ohio State")
UTALong <- beststacked |> filter(Team == "University of Texas at Austin")
WFLong <- beststacked |> filter(Team == "Wake Forest")

ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=beststacked, aes(x=reorder(Team, Total),, weight=Total, fill=Outcome)) +
scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Games", 
    values  = c("lightgrey", "darkgrey"), 
    labels = c("Wins", "Losses")
    ) +
  new_scale_fill() + 
  geom_bar(data=OSLong, aes(x=reorder(Team, Total),, weight=Total, fill=Outcome)) +
scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Games", 
    values  = c("red", "blue"), 
    labels = c("Wins", "Losses")
    ) +
  new_scale_fill() + 
  geom_bar(data=UTALong, aes(x=reorder(Team, Total),, weight=Total, fill=Outcome)) +
scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Games", 
    values  = c("red", "blue"), 
    labels = c("Wins", "Losses")
    ) +
  new_scale_fill() + 
  geom_bar(data=WFLong, aes(x=reorder(Team, Total),, weight=Total, fill=Outcome)) +
scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Games", 
    values  = c("red", "blue"), 
    labels = c("Wins", "Losses")
    ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x="College", 
    y="Total Points",
    title="The #1 College Team", 
    subtitle="Using data from the past 4 years to see which team has had the highest amount of points in 
the Women's Tennis League.", 
    caption="Source: ITA | By Halle Winfrey"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )

As we see in the graph, Ohio State has consistently scored very high with over 150 points from the past four seasons while losing 12 out of the 133 total games played. Second place goes to University of Texas at Austin, who is pretty close to reaching Ohio State. And the third place winner is Wake Forest falling not too far behind UTA, and also has the least amount of games lost from the top three.

Now that we know the top colleges, what about the top conferences? Which conference has had the highest points from the past seasons, and what are the point differences between each conference?

To find the top conferences in the league, we’ll use the same data from the first chart and focus on the conference of each team.

Now to see the highest scoring conferences, and their total scores.

Code 
conf <- womens |> 
  group_by(Conference) |> 
  summarize(total_points = sum(Points)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(is.na(Conference) == FALSE)

SEC <- conf |> filter(Conference == "Southeastern Conference")
B12 <- conf |> filter(Conference == "Big 12 Conference")
B10 <- conf |> filter(Conference == "Big Ten Conference")
ACC <- conf |> filter(Conference == "Atlantic Coast Conference")

ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=conf, aes(x=reorder(Conference, total_points), weight=total_points), fill="grey") +
  geom_bar(data=SEC, aes(x=reorder(Conference, total_points), weight=total_points), fill="blue") +
  geom_bar(data=B12, aes(x=reorder(Conference, total_points), weight=total_points), fill="red") +
  geom_bar(data=B10, aes(x=reorder(Conference, total_points), weight=total_points), fill="purple") +
  geom_bar(data=ACC, aes(x=reorder(Conference, total_points), weight=total_points), fill="darkgreen") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x="", 
    y="Total Points", 
    title="The Top Conferences and Their Scores", 
    subtitle="Using the same data to total up each team's scores within their conference and seeing which 
one has the most points.", 
    caption="Source: ITA | By Halle Winfrey"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )

From the chart, our top conference for Women’s Tennis is the Southeastern Conference; with a combined score of over 2,000 points. The number two spot goes to the Atlantic Coast Conference which has over 1,600 points. Coming in third place is the Big 12 Conference with just over 1,100 total points. And the fourth best conference is the Big Ten with a little over 1,100 points as well. The Big 12 and Big 10 are very close in rankings with only a 41.45 point difference.

Seeing the top colleges and the top conferences is really interesting, but there is also a question of who the top individual players are, and also, what their scores look like.

The data from the Intercollegiate Tennis Association shows each player from each season with their points, along with their wins and losses.

Let’s see who the best overall player from the combined seasons is.

Code 
singles <- read_csv("Women's Tennis Singles - Sheet1.csv")

bestsingles <- singles |> filter(Points > 13)
LP <- bestsingles |> filter(Players == "Lucciana Perez")
MS <- bestsingles |> filter(Players == "Mary Stoiana")
FC <- bestsingles |> filter(Players == "Fiona Crawley")
DV <- bestsingles |> filter(Players == "Dasha Vidmanova")

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data=bestsingles, aes(x=Season, y=Points, group=Players), color="grey") +
  geom_line(data=LP, aes(x=Season, y=Points, group=1), color="purple") + 
  geom_line(data=MS, aes(x=Season, y=Points, group=1), color="blue") +
  geom_line(data=FC, aes(x=Season, y=Points, group=1), color="darkred") +
  geom_text_repel(data=LP |> filter(Season == max(Season)), aes(x=Season, y=Points, group=Team, label=Players)) + 
  geom_point(data=LP |> filter(Season == max(Season)), aes(x=Season, y=Points)) +   
  geom_text_repel(data=MS |> filter(Season == max(Season)), aes(x=Season, y=Points, group=Team, label=Players)) + 
  geom_point(data=MS |> filter(Season == max(Season)), aes(x=Season, y=Points)) + 
  geom_text_repel(data=FC |> filter(Season == max(Season)), aes(x=Season, y=Points, group=Team, label=Players)) + 
  geom_point(data=FC |> filter(Season == max(Season)), aes(x=Season, y=Points)) + 
  labs(
    y="Total Points", 
    x="",
    title="The Best Players from the Best Conferences", 
    subtitle="Taking individual players' points from the past four seasons and seeing who the best college tennis player is.", 
    caption="Source: ITA | By Halle Winfrey"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 17, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )

The number one player from the combined seasons is Lucciana Perez from Texas A&M University, with a score of 76.65. Since there are only points from one season, this score is only for the 2025-2026 season, but Perez still has the most points. The second place spot is Mary Stoiana, who has consistently scored very high over the past four seasons. Ending with our third place spot, which is Fiona Crawley who played in two seasons from 2022 to 2024.

Each school, conference, and individual player from the data, come close in points but we still see differences in their overall scores along with their wins and losses.
